scenes.heading: SCD Type 1
scenes.narration: A Slowly Changing Dimension of Type 1 simply overwrites old attribute values with new ones.

scenes.heading: How Type 1 behaves
bullets: Updates replace the existing value in place.
No history of the previous value is kept.
The table stays small and simple.
Best for corrections, not meaningful change.
scenes.narration: With Type 1, when an attribute changes you overwrite it and the old value is gone. That keeps the dimension small and queries straightforward. It fits corrections like fixing a misspelled name, where the past value has no analytical value worth preserving.

scenes.heading: Overwriting in place
scenes.code:
UPDATE dim_customer
SET    email      = 'new@example.com',
       updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
WHERE  customer_key = 42;
scenes.narration: This update simply replaces the email for a single customer. There is no second row and no history, so the warehouse instantly reflects the new value. The trade-off is that any report run before the change can no longer be reproduced exactly.

scenes.heading: Type 1 vs Type 2
scenes.narration: Type 1 favors simplicity and treats changes as corrections to forget. Type 2 preserves every version so you can analyze the past as it truly was. Choosing between them comes down to whether history has business value or is just noise.

scenes.text: SCD Type 1 overwrites values with no history, ideal for corrections where the old value carries no analytical meaning.
scenes.narration: Use Type 1 when the past value is simply wrong and no one will ever need to see it again.
